scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9127: the NOC believes an OSPF virtual-link in the core
"collapsed" after a router reload, leaving a non-backbone area cut off from the
backbone -- they think traffic that has to transit the area-1 virtual-link (the
r4<->r8 path that stitches Area 2 to Area 0) is now black-holed. They want the
broken virtual-link found and re-established. Please confirm the fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF virtual-links are intact: r4 and r8
  both hold their `area 1 virtual-link` config, the virtual adjacency is up, and
  every non-backbone area remains attached to Area 0. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, exercising a path that depends on the
  converged multi-area fabric. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of a virtual-link collapse that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r4-virtual-link-removed / kath5-r8-virtual-link-removed, where one IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a collapsed OSPF
virtual-link leaving an area unreachable -- is NOT reproducible: the r4<->r8
virtual adjacency is up (both endpoints still configure `area 1 virtual-link`,
each pointing at the other's router-id), and the transit chain stitching the
non-backbone areas to Area 0 is intact. End-to-end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone + virtual-links + the EIGRP
domain, which it could not if a virtual-link on the path had collapsed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the virtual-links are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the virtual-link state
(both endpoints present, adjacency up), confirms the affected area's prefixes are
still in the RIB, and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a collapsed virtual-link or a stranded area --
blaming r4/r8 or re-adding a virtual-link that is already there -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The NOC ticket's premise is incorrect. The OSPF virtual-link between r4 (router-ID 14.1.4.1) and r8 (router-ID 18.1.4.1), traversing Area 0.0.0.1 as the transit area, is fully operational. Both endpoints confirm VLINK0 is administratively up, in Point-to-Point state, with the remote peer in Full/DROther adjacency state and an adjacent-neighbor count of 1 on both sides. The virtual-link has been stable since lab startup — the slightly shorter VL uptime (~1m43s) versus the underlying Area 1 adjacencies (~2m07s) is normal: the VL can only form after the transit-area adjacencies converge first.

Area 2 (r8's loopback stub networks 18.1.x.1/32 and eth1 segment 80.0.0.0/8) is not cut off from the backbone. r8 is functioning correctly as an ABR: it injects type-3 summary LSAs for its Area 2 prefixes into the backbone, and those routes appear in the RIB of every backbone router checked — r3 sees 18.1.x.1/32 at cost 30 and 80.0.0.0/8 at cost 40 via r4, and r4 sees the same Area 2 routes at cost 20 via r5. The LSDB shows both r4 and r8 advertising correct inter-area summary LSAs, demonstrating proper ABR operation on both ends of the virtual-link.

All five non-backbone areas (1, 2, 3, 4) have confirmed, active backbone connectivity. There is no routing black-hole and no forwarding anomaly attributable to virtual-link failure. The network is healthy; the NOC ticket is a false positive based on an erroneous post-reload assumption.

**Corrective fix:** No configuration change is required. The virtual-link is up; no re-establishment is needed. The NOC can close ticket #9127 as a false alarm.
